checks.name: client-cursor-contract-six-variants
checks.summary: The client contract was settled by measurement, in a check of its own, over the local emulator on a requirements collection of 5 documents ordered by cloudfirestore.DocumentID (unfiltered row count 5, collection resource path projects/agentic-loop-test/databases/(default)/documents/installations/<key>/requirements, first document key cmVxdWlyZW1lbnQtMQ). All six variants, with verdicts. (1) COLLECTION PATH JOINED TO THE DOCUMENT ID: ERROR, 0 rows, `code = InvalidArgument ... Document parent name "..." lacks "/" at index 203` with the installations/<key>/requirements pair appearing twice. (2) BARE DOCUMENT ID: OK, 4 rows. (3) THE LAST ROW'S *DocumentRef: OK, 4 rows -- the identical page. (4) THE *DocumentSnapshot: OK, 4 rows -- the identical page. (5) A FABRICATED DOCUMENT ID no document has (PathKey of "requirement-does-not-exist"): OK, 0 rows -- accepted, not refused, which is the boundary A9's refusal test must not cross. (6) A *DocumentRef BUILT FROM A DIFFERENT COLLECTION of the same installation (the first document of installations/<key>/events): SILENTLY ACCEPTED, OK, 5 rows -- the WHOLE UNFILTERED PAGE, the cursor having no effect at all. Every one of the six verdicts agrees with dp-v2-079 d1 and d2; nothing was escalated. The mechanism was confirmed in the client's own source rather than inferred: cloud.google.com/go/firestore@v1.25.0/query.go, Query.fieldValuesToCursorValues, builds the ReferenceValue for a string cursor under an isDocumentID order as q.path + "/" + docID where q.path is the collection's FULL resource name, and carries an unimplemented `// TODO(jba): error if document ref does not belong to the right collection.` at query.go:967 -- the exact branch variant 6 goes through. The neighbouring docSnapshotToCursorValues, by contrast, DOES compare ds.Ref.Parent.Path with q.path and errors on a mismatch, which is why the snapshot form is the checked one and the ref form is the weaker guard. That is the measurement that decides the design: variants 2, 3 and 4 return the identical page, variant 1 is refused, and variant 6 is silently accepted and resets the page to everything, so the BARE DOCUMENT ID is taken -- it is the client's documented contract, it needs no extra read, and it fails loudly rather than silently. This measurement also came from the temporary probe file described in the reproduction check and was deleted with it.

checks.name: requirement-cursor-walk-covers-every-row-once
checks.summary: A6, the outcome test, on the Firestore adapter under the name that also exists in internal/store/memory: TestThePageCursorTheCallerWasHandedIsAcceptedByTheNextPageUntilEveryRequirementIsCoveredOnce. It seeds N=7 Requirements (N strictly greater than 3), drives Service.ListRequirementsPage -- so the opaque v1 cursor envelope is exercised and not merely the port -- and feeds every returned next_cursor into the next call until a page returns none. VERDICT: `--- PASS` for both sub-walks under `ok github.com/takushi/agentic-loop-foundation/v2/internal/store/firestore 1.857s` with -race, and the same two names PASS inside the full `make component-store-firestore` run. It walks to the LAST page at page_size=1 (7 pages) and then re-walks the whole Backlog at page_size=2, which does NOT divide 7 (pages of 2,2,2,1), which is what catches an off-by-one in the exclusive boundary. Asserted: every non-terminal page carries exactly page_size rows; the terminal page carries NO cursor and 1..page_size rows; the walk terminates within a bound derived from N (len(seeded)/pageSize + 2) and never on a timer, no sleep, no goroutine, no wall clock; and the concatenation of every page equals the seeded ids as a MULTISET -- each seeded id seen exactly once and no extra id seen, so a duplicate, an omission, a refusal and a non-terminating walk are all failures. NO ORDER IS ASSERTED, and the test says why in its own comment: base64url is not order-preserving, the seeded ids are chosen so the two adapters genuinely disagree (raw req-aa < req-at while base64url gives cmVxLWFh > cmVxLWF0, and the measured first page here is indeed req-at, not req-aa), so an order assertion would pass on memory and fail on Firestore for a reason that has nothing to do with the cursor (dp-v2-079 d4). The test is PROVEN able to see the defect it fixes: on the pre-change tree the identical file failed with `page 1 with cursor "eyJ2IjoidjEiLCJhZnRlciI6InJlcS1hdCJ9": rpc error: code = InvalidArgument ... lacks "/" at index 193` at page_size=1 and the same at page_size=2.
